slides.title: Numbers, Shapes, and Measurement
bullets: Prepare to read, discuss and write
slides.narration: Welcome to Grade 3 English, Unit 8: Numbers, Shapes, and Measurement. In this unit you use English to talk about maths in real life. You count and name big numbers, all the way up to one million. You learn the words addition, subtraction, multiplication and division. You measure the size, height, weight and distance of things around you, using words like metre and centimetre. You also hunt for straight lines and repeating patterns. Maths is everywhere: in the market, in the kitchen and on the way to school. By the end you will solve a number puzzle, just like Amal and Sami do in this unit's story. In this short lecture, preview the key ideas and prepare for the independent lesson.

slides.title: What you will achieve
bullets: Read and say big numbers, up to one million.
Use the maths words addition, subtraction, multiplication and division.
Measure the size, height, weight and distance of things around you.
slides.narration: By the end of this unit, you will be able to read and say big numbers, up to one million. You will also use the maths words addition, subtraction, multiplication and division. You will also measure the size, height, weight and distance of things around you. Keep these goals in mind as you work.

slides.title: Words to learn
slides.narration: Your vocabulary work begins with these words: number, million, fact, pattern, straight, addition. Listen to each word, look at what it means, and try to use it when you talk and write.

slides.title: Read and think
bullets: Point to the words that show it
slides.narration: The reading sequence includes Maths Is Everywhere and A Pattern Poem. Read slowly, look at the pictures, and find the big idea in each text. When you answer a question, point to the words that show it.

Try it in your own sentences
slides.narration: The first language focus is Present Simple and Imperatives. The Present Simple tells about things that happen often or facts that are always true, like “The sun rises in the east.” An imperative is a command or instruction, like “Measure the height.” Both help us speak and write clearly, especially in maths. Look at the examples, then try the pattern in your own sentences.

slides.title: Use English for a real purpose
bullets: Say it, write it, make it better
slides.narration: In speaking, you will complete Speaking 1 — Measure and Tell. Say your ideas clearly and listen to your partner. In writing, you will draw, trace, copy or write, then check your work with a grown-up or the AI tutor.

slides.title: You are ready to begin
bullets: Activities, quiz and optional live sessions
slides.narration: You are ready to begin. Start with the words, then the reading and the questions, then the grammar, speaking and writing. Ask the AI tutor for help any time, and bring your questions to a live session too if you join one.
